record.context_brief: Ergodic compact-group actions on Neumann algebras
record.original_question: Let σ: G → Aut(M) be an ergodic action of a compact group G on a Neumann algebra M. Must M necessarily be finite?

evidence.quote: Let an action σ: G → Aut(M) of the compact group G on the Neumann algebra M be ergodic. Is M necessarily finite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a von Neumann algebra and let $G$ be a compact (Hausdorff topological) group. Suppose $\sigma : G \to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$ is an action of $G$ on $M$ by $*$-automorphisms which is continuous in the sense that for every $x \in M$ and every $\varphi \in M_*$ the map $g \mapsto \varphi(\sigma_g(x))$ is continuous on $G$. The action $\sigma$ is called ergodic if the fixed-point algebra
$$M^\sigma = \{x \in M : \sigma_g(x) = x \text{ for all } g \in G\}$$
equals $\mathbb{C}\,1_M$. 

Question: Whenever such an ergodic action of a compact group on a von Neumann algebra $M$ exists, must $M$ be a finite von Neumann algebra (i.e. admit a faithful normal tracial state, equivalently a separating family of finite normal traces)?
artifact.category_tag: ergodic actions on von Neumann algebras
artifact.status_search_result: Høegh-Krohn, Landstad and Størmer (Annals of Math., 1981, "Compact ergodic groups of automorphisms") proved that if a compact group acts ergodically on a von Neumann algebra, then the unique invariant state is a trace and the algebra is finite (in fact finite and injective). So the question is answered affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Growth rates of dimensional invariants of compact quantum groups and a theorem of Hoegh-Krohn, Landstad and Stormer
status_evidence.snippet: A theorem of Høegh-Krohn, Landstad and Størmer states that compact groups admit ergodic actions only on tracial von Neumann algebras, with the invariant state necessarily being a trace; in particular the algebra is finite.
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative answer: ergodic compact-group action forces M to be finite (and the invariant state is a trace).

status_evidence.title: Ergodic actions of compact groups on operator algebras (Inventiones)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational work on ergodic actions of compact groups on operator algebras, building on the Høegh-Krohn–Landstad–Størmer theorem.
status_evidence.claim: The classical theory establishes finiteness of the algebra under ergodic compact-group action.
